description: The open-source managed agent platform. A self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API.

summary.one_liner: Omnara is an open-source, self-hostable managed agent platform for running AI agents on any model and any machine, with tools, secrets, permissions, and streaming built in.
keywords: run ai agents on my machine
use_cases: Self-host an AI agent platform for a team
Launch agents on laptops, VMs, or cloud sandboxes from an app
Run long-lived agents that survive restarts and machine disconnects
Trigger agents from Slack, Discord, GitHub, or cron schedules
Keep agent run history in your own Postgres for analytics or evals
Build PR review or incident investigation agents
how_to_run: npx omnara agents launch --file agent.yaml --name "Machine assistant" --message "Report this machine's operating system and free disk space."
notable: Self-hosted alternative to Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API, with any model supported
Machines connect outbound via the omnarad daemon, so no inbound ports or SSH keys are needed
Sandboxes from eleven providers, and an agent can use several machines and move between them
Every agent step is saved in Postgres, so agents resume after crashes or restarts
Per-tool permissions (run, ask, or block) enforced by the platform, with approvals waiting on a person
caveats: Self-hosted local defaults are intentionally insecure; a real deployment needs the self-hosting guide and configuration reference
A new self-hosted instance has no models or machines until you add them in the console
Sandboxes require the instance to have a public URL when self-hosting
Omnara Cloud charges pay-as-you-go for its own models and sandboxes; pricing is separate from the free self-hosted option
